summary:
# NOTES: *The Slave of Silence* by F. M. White (1906, Little, Brown & Co.)

Single novel, no separate BOOK headings. 40 chapters (I–XL). Front matter: Frontispiece "Nothing daunted, the pair made a rush at Berrington who fired right and left" (p.191); other plate "Richford stood there shaking and quivering with passion" (p.49); "The police officer looked suspiciously at the figure" (p.107). Ad pages at end for E. Phillips Oppenheim novels (A Maker of History, The Master Mummer, A Prince of Sinners, Anna the Adventuress, Mysterious Mr. Sabin, The Yellow Crayon, The Traitors, The Betrayal, A Millionaire of Yesterday, The Man and His Kingdom). Ignore for plot.

## Cast
- **Beatrice Darryll** (later Mrs. Richford), 22, dark-clad, blue eyes, warm-ripe hair. Daughter of Sir Charles.
- **Sir Charles Darryll**, baronet, "boyish," gambler/speculator in a City company; crooked. Wife (Beatrice's mother) deceased; Beatrice inherited honour from her.
- **Stephen Richford**, millionaire, heavy, thick lip, shifty small eyes, prize-fighter look; drinks secretly; father also crooked. Ultimately fraudster; firm "Richford & Co." collapses; warrant; dies falling from bridge.
- **Mark Ventmore**, painter, Beatrice's former fiancé; father disowned him for preferring art to the City. Later reconciled; father is rich, sends cheque/allowance £1,500 then £5000/yr to Mark.
- **Colonel Philip "Phil" Berrington**, brilliant soldier, long leave, melancholy, former Indian service; friend of Mark's father; loves Mary Sartoris (Grey) since engagement years earlier.
- **Mary Sartoris / Mary Grey**, grey-haired at ~31 (age "barely thirty" / "thirty-one"), brown eyes, "grey lady," "Slave of Silence"/"Slave of the Bond"; sister of Carl Sartoris; devoted, self-sacrificing.
- **Carl Sartoris** (real name **Carl Grey**), crippled invalid in bath-chair, pale, fair hair, dark vivid eyes, mocking, cruel, electrical gadgets; sinful; ex-Civil Service expelled; dies of internal bleeding after motor accident.
- **Inspector Field**, Scotland Yard, tall/stern-faced, shrewd; ex-soldier-type; wife and family.
- **Adeline**, Beatrice's maid; sweetheart in a shop.
- **Lady Adela Rashborough** (Adela), pretty, blue-eyed, heartless; husband **Lord Rashborough** ("Frank"), open-air man, hates gambling.
- **Dr. Andrews**, doctor who doubted death; **Dr. Oswin**, family doctor.
- **Countess de la Moray** (= "Cora") and **General Gastang** (= "Reggie"), swindlers; Reggie is "Reggie," Cora is "Cora."
- **Bentwood** (Dr. James Bentwood), big, red-faced drunk, ex-army surgeon, Eastern drugs/poisons, buried-alive experiment; drugged Sir Charles.
- **Mr. Marius**, hotel manager of Royal Palace Hotel.
- **Macklin**, policeman at Wandsworth, ex-soldier under Berrington.
- **Catton**, night watchman; **Benwort**, hall porter (bound, struck); **Saunders**, Field's man.
- **Violet Decie** (Hon.), ward of Sir Charles, actress "Adela Vane" at Comedy Opera House; once engaged to Carl Grey; saved by Frank Leviter who died.
- **Lady Parkstone**, Violet's aunt.
- **George Fleming**, lawyer, Lincoln's Inn Fields firm (George Fleming & Co.).
- **Acton**, disgraced law stationer/forger, bought stamped parchment.
- **Countess de la Moray** had drugging scent.
- **Rajah of Ahbad** (renegade, Eton/Oxford educated, shady) — involved, present at Audley Place.
- **Lord Edward Decie**, deceased friend of Sir Charles; Violet's father.
- **Mrs. Beacon Light**, alias of the grey lady in hotel register.

## Story Events in Order
1. Night before wedding, Royal Palace Hotel. Beatrice wears black. Sir Charles (in debt; City company failure; two watchers outside) forces her to marry Richford for £5,000 cheque/money to save him. Beatrice once loved Mark; wrote to Mark in Venice; letter miscarried. Grey lady (Slave of the Bond) appears in Beatrice's dining-room, grey silk dress, brown eyes, white/grey hair.
2. Dinner. Colonel Berrington beside Beatrice. Waiter gives wine card No. 74 with pencilled note "In the little conservatory beyond the drawing-room. Soon as possible" in Mark's handwriting. Richford: "Ain't they worth one single kiss?" (later).  Mark disguised as waiter; reunion in conservatory; Mark: "For God's sake don't say I have come too late!"
3. Mark learns Sir Charles's schemes and tells of seeing grey lady in Paris theatre. Richford sulks. Mark sleeps in room near Sir Charles's; sees grey lady leave Sir Charles's sitting-room; door locked. Mark wakes after 11, room broken down at midday.
4. Wedding morning: Adeline; Richford arrives shaking; gives Rockmartin diamonds (£40,000), Beatrice refuses kiss. Lord Rashborough: "appointment at Tattersall's at half-past two." Wedding ceremony: Mark interrupts at altar; "Sir Charles was found in his bed quite dead."
5. Hotel; Dr. Andrews says dead ~4 hrs; Richford arrives; Beatrice finds telegram (grey paper) addressed to Richford in father's room. Letter by "Mrs. Beacon Light" (grey lady) to Sir Charles found, delivered by hand.
6. Berrington identifies grey lady's handwriting. Mark finds visitors' book: "Mrs. Beacon Light." Inspector; inquest set. Beatrice confronts Richford: telegram proves he saw body; she threatens to tell. Richford lunches; salt bullet on steak (the "salt sign"). Berrington follows Richford in hansom to No. 100, Audley Place, Wandsworth Common (Carl Sartoris, bath-chair).
7. Berrington, policeman Macklin (No. 14 Audley Place is Colonel Foley). Richford meets Sartoris: discusses death; forbids inquest. Sartoris: "there must be no inquest on the body of Sir Charles Darryll."
8. Beatrice to Lady Rashborough—rejected. Sells jewellery (~£200). Countess de la Moray (drugger) and General Gastang appear; Beatrice finds Countess and Richford in her locked room; wax on Countess's fingers; wax impression of seal; Countess's scent drugs Beatrice.
9. Next morning: Dr. Andrews and inspector: body disappeared. Beatrice tells Field of Countess/General; Field searches. Night watchman Catton and hall porter Benwort missing. Blood on carpet; hall porter found bound, gagged in Rajah of Ahbad's suite; night watchman Catton hit on head. "lady in grey" fetched him. Black cab with pale lame man and trunk; cabman.
10. Berrington: "The lame man of No. 100 Audley Place!" Field and Berrington reason; Beatrice gives full account. Berrington/Field to Wandsworth in disguise (sailors from ship Severn); Macklin. House apparently closed; warm kitchen; Rajah arrives, Countess/Cora and General/Reggie appear; Richford; Sartoris, Bentwood. Body unwrapped on table. Grey lady ("Mary") appears; Berrington reveals himself. Mary: "Carl is my brother." Berrington struck; overpowered.
11. Field fetches police, house empty. Field later learns Adela Vane = Violet Decie; Berrington's flashing message from upper window; Field to Edward Street, Borough. Field saves Violet from theatre fire at Comedy; Violet = actress Adela Vane; Field meets Cora & Reggie at Edward Street.
12. Berrington taken; Sartoris shocks him with electricity; Berrington writes letter (forged by Sartoris) to Beatrice; overheard Sartoris–Richford quarrel; Burmese torturers; Berrington frees Sartoris; ruby mines; Sir Charles's "rich man" secret.
13. Richford disguised as elderly clergyman; sells; Richford/Reggie/Cora plot; Beatrice takes diamonds to jewellers? No: she deposits at Hilton (Bond St)? (Beatrice walks toward jewellers in Bond St, goes to Wandsworth). Mary follows; Beatrice meets Sartoris.
14. Fleming; deed "C.D." signature; stamp dated 4.4.'93; Somerset House numbers 44791; Acton forged; Richford's fleet; Mark's fleeing; Field & Mark at house; raid on Edward Street; Bentwood arrested; motor car.
15. Shootout in dining-room; Berrington rescues Beatrice; Reggie and Cora arrested; Richford killed in motor car crash on bridge; Sartoris dies of bleeding rib in lung ("Feel my hands").
16. Sir Charles found alive, disguised (drugged by Bentwood; used Sartoris's house; signed deed). Mark's father (rich, grey eyes) buys concessions; Sir Charles gets £500 and 'cheque'. Berrington marries Mary; Mark & Beatrice wait six months; Mary's final line: "thank God no longer the Slave of Silence!"

## Key Quotes/Details
- Sir Charles: "Honour thy father..."; Mark: "Am I too late?"
- Telegram: addressed to Richford; ~10 a.m. grey paper; date and day.
- Cab, Tattersall's, half past two; diamonds £40,000 ("Rockmartin gems").
- Doctor: body dead ~4 hours. Bentwood's "Melanyl" ink on collar (Beatrice marked collars with Melanyl at 4:30 p.m.).
- Concessions: Ruby mines in Burmah; deed dated 4.4.'93 (sold by Somerset House stamps No. 44791); signature genuine.
